# Model card: Job description drafting

| | |
|---|---|
| Purpose | Draft a job description in English and Arabic from a recruiter's brief. |
| Workflow | hire |
| Code | `pairly_hire.drafting.draft_job_description` |
| Prompt | `hire_jd_draft` version `v1`, file SHA-256 `2c5e292714a29399...` |
| Output schema | `JobDescriptionDraft` |
| Model tiers, cheapest first | `small` (anthropic `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`, openai `gpt-6-luna`) then `large` (anthropic `claude-sonnet-5-5`, openai `gpt-6.1-sol`) |
| Temperature | 0.0 |
| Output token limit | 4096 |
| Confidence threshold to accept | none |

## Inputs

The recruiter's brief for the role. No candidate data.

## Outputs

A `JobDescriptionDraft` (English and Arabic text). Deterministic inclusive-language and sanity checks then run on the draft and are shown next to it.

## Human oversight

A recruiter reads, edits and saves the text. Publishing a job is a `publish` action that needs a second factor. Nothing the model writes is published by itself.

## Limits

* Can be generic or miss what makes the role specific.
* The inclusive-language check is pattern based and can miss subtle wording.
* Without a model (no key, no recording, over budget) the recruiter writes the text; the route answers with a plain message.
* Every call is logged in `model_calls` (prompt version and hash, model, inputs, output, tokens, cost) and fails closed: no model means a person does the step.

Structural checks only (`python -m evals.structural`), on the committed recordings: scripted answers, not model output. They say whether every recorded output fits the schema, holds no banned content or em dash, passes the component's own deterministic check and points only at its input. They are not quality judgments: how good a draft is needs a live model and people.
